title: Can a Gas Cloud Birth a Star?

segments.text: Could a cloud of gas birth a star?
A massive cloud of gas and dust starts collapsing, breaking into smaller pieces.
Each fragment spins, forming a hidden protostar that glows in infrared.
Typical giant molecular clouds stretch about one hundred light‑years across, yet they shrink like a collapsing pillow.
Gravity pulls harder on denser bits, turning them into separate cores that heat up.
Those cores keep sucking up material, growing hotter and brighter.
All that begins with a cloud of gas can become a star.
